headline: The head of the International Monetary Fund warned in Bangkok that the world economy leans heavily on AI investment and asked what would happen if it faltered.
score_reason: Official warning with named speaker, but general and not new in substance; facts support the pool score.
importance_line: Governments and households in weaker economies are exposed if AI spending slows, but the warning is general and the IMF gives no date or size for such a risk.
summary: The Nation Thailand reports that Kristalina Georgieva, managing director of the International Monetary Fund, told a debate at the IMF and World Bank meetings in Bangkok on Thursday 15 Oct 2026 that the world economy is "like on one leg", increasingly reliant on AI investment, and urged governments to rebuild financial buffers. She said the IMF's 3.1% global growth forecast for 2026 hides widening gaps, with the United States, China and India gaining from AI while other economies struggle with inflation, debt and higher energy costs.
notes: The pool item is MarketWatch's story (blocked, 401). It was not read, and its exact wording may cover a different Georgieva remark; The Nation Thailand's report of her 15 Oct debate remarks is used and credited instead.
